column3: Directly joins Allah's knowledge of heaven-and-earth unseen with sight of human deeds.
Frames the heavens and earth as wholly God's, adding sovereignty to their hidden domain.
The closing attribute "All-Knowing" is general and adds little beyond the focus.
Most closely repeats knowledge of heavens, earth, secrecy, publicity, and what chests contain.
The immediate continuation tests rival claims against creation in earth and the heavens.
Healing believers' chests concerns inward states but not divine knowledge of them.
Details matters known only to Allah, including wombs, tomorrow's gain, and the place of death.
The immediate continuation shows God sustaining heavens and earth against displacement.
Absence from the Fire does not clarify cosmic unseen knowledge or inward contents.
Explicitly assigns the unseen of heavens and earth to God, then stresses the nearness of the Hour.
States that every hidden thing in heaven and earth is fixed in a clarifying record.
The plea to expand a chest offers only a limited inward-body parallel.
Directly pairs concealed and spoken utterance with knowledge of what is within chests.
The local description of God as aware and seeing supports the surrounding disclosure theme generally.
Links final return and deeds with God's knowledge of inner chests.
God's knowledge of chests grounds discernment of falsehood from truth in a contested claim.
The description of Garden adornment adds no relation to hidden knowledge.
Places clear signs within the chests of those given knowledge, a human counterpart to inward content.
Explicitly gives God the unseen of heavens and earth and emphasizes His complete sight and hearing.
God holding birds in the sky is a limited counterpart to the following holding of heavens and earth.
Challenges people who claim possession of the unseen, contrasting their claim with divine knowledge.
Connects God's unseen of heavens and earth to the return of every affair and awareness of deeds.
The local conclusion combines heavens and earth with God's knowledge and power over past outcomes.
Names God knower of unseen and witnessed reality, extending the hidden/open boundary.
Pairs knowledge of heaven-and-earth unseen with what people reveal and conceal.
The punishment of earlier deniers does not add to the focus's knowledge claim.
Chest expansion is an inward-state parallel but lacks the focus's knowing relation.
Universal praise in heavens and earth with God knowing deeds is a broad cosmic counterpart.
The messengers yield their knowledge before the One who fully knows unseen things.
General divine knowledge supports accountability but adds no unseen or chest-specific element.
Knowledge of chests explains a protective vision, a narrower practical application of inward knowledge.
Earthly succession and disbelief do not clarify the focus's knowledge claim.
The knower of chests accompanies the alternation of night and day, a broad cosmic setting.
Final reporting of deeds is explicitly grounded in knowledge of what chests contain.
The punishment description does not develop unseen knowledge or inward contents.
Whispering in human chests identifies an inward arena without the knowing relation.
Human knowledge lost in old age contrasts limited creaturely knowledge with divine knowledge.
Names God as knower of unseen and witnessed reality, though it lacks the cosmic and chest pairing.
Future knowing after heedlessness does not illuminate the focus's present divine knowledge.
Warns against asking beyond one's knowledge, a limited contrast to divine complete knowledge.
The return of evil plotting to its authors does not add to the knowledge statement.
Directly joins what chests conceal and what people disclose under God's knowledge.
Teaching the Quran alone does not clarify the focus's unseen or chest language.
Gratitude after sorrow's removal does not develop the focus.
Restricts understanding of parables to the learned, a remote human-knowledge counterpart.
Attributes revelation to the One who knows secret matters in heavens and earth.
Creation of heavens and earth in truth supplies only a broad cosmic frame.
Knower of unseen and witnessed reality repeats the attribute but adds no further relation.
God knows every utterance in heaven and earth, extending knowledge from inward contents to speech.
The local ending presents delayed accountability under God's sight of servants.
Revelation sent with God's knowledge gives a limited disclosure counterpart.
Unequivocally reserves knowledge of the unseen in heavens and earth to Allah alone.
Human need and divine self-sufficiency do not clarify hidden knowledge.
The creation cycle and earth's revival include human ignorance but do not develop the focus directly.
God's ownership of heavens and earth is a broad companion to the focus's cosmic scope.
Creation in truth and human ignorance do not clarify hidden or inward knowledge.
Specifies that God knows furtive looks as well as what chests hide.
Combines divine presence across heavens and earth with knowledge of secret, open, and earned acts.
The local plea from punishment does not add to the focus's knowledge claim.
Ignorance of coming punishment does not clarify God's knowledge of hidden things.
Cosmic ownership, present human condition, return, and full knowledge form an accountability expansion.
The contrast of punishment and reward does not develop unseen knowledge.
Removal of rancor from chests is an inward-content parallel without knowing or disclosure.
Rejects teaching God while affirming His knowledge of everything in heavens and earth.
The dismissive labels do not clarify divine knowledge.
People defer disputed duration to God's fuller knowledge, a narrow creaturely limitation parallel.
Depicts efforts to hide in chests and coverings as unable to escape knowledge of secret and open.
Reward, increase, forgiveness, and thanks do not add to the focus.
God's knowledge of what people conceal and disclose consoles against their speech.
Divine ownership of heavens and earth is already covered without the focus's unseen dimension.
The revelation's divine source does not clarify hidden knowledge.
The promise of a knowledgeable son is unrelated to God's cosmic and inward knowledge.
Covenant obedience is placed under God's knowledge of what chests contain.
Future questioning about the reminder does not develop the focus.
Human ignorance of revealed limits contrasts limited knowledge with God's knowing attribute.
Knowledge accompanies control of provision in heavens and earth but remains general.
Unearthing graves begins a disclosure image but does not yet name inner contents.
God's hearing and knowledge in seeking refuge do not clarify the focus's themes.
Sacred institutions are said to show that God knows heavens, earth, and all things.
Plotting and mountains supply no meaningful knowledge-of-unseen relation.
The future warning of knowing adds no connection after stronger knowledge passages.
Directly joins concealed and revealed chest contents with knowledge of heavens and earth.
Final divine expertise supports disclosure but is less specific than earlier chest passages.
Contrasts limited human knowledge with God's fuller knowledge of guidance and error.
God's encompassing knowledge and preservation of heavens and earth deepen the cosmic scope.
The repeated future warning of knowing adds no specific relation.
Exposes concealed hostility behind public professions through God's knowledge of chests.
Divine awareness of the Prophet's constricted chest is a particular emotional application.
Names God knower of unseen and witnessed reality within creation, dominion, and final return.
Reverence in the unseen and a returning heart offer a human response, not divine knowledge itself.
Heaven-and-earth belonging to God is a broad sovereignty parallel already represented.
Pretending not to know revelation does not clarify the focus's divine knowledge.
God's expertise in deeds at death is a narrow accountability counterpart.
Future exposure of associators does not add to the focus's hidden-knowledge claim.
The earth as a resting place has no relevant relation.
The magnitude of an oath known by hearers does not clarify divine knowledge.
God's exclusive guardianship and power do not develop the focus.
Requested interpretation and human learning are unrelated to divine knowledge of the unseen.
Inheritance rules ending in an attribute of knowledge add no focused relation.
Future identification of a liar does not clarify the focus.
Nothing in heaven or earth is hidden from Allah, directly extending the focus's cosmic unseen claim.
The keys of the unseen and exhaustive knowledge of land, sea, and every hidden event closely parallel the focus.
God's knowledge of good in hearts gives a concrete inward application of the focus's knowledge of chest contents.
No deed or smallest particle is absent from God's knowledge in earth or heaven, expanding its exhaustive scope.
Explicitly names God knower of unseen and witnessed reality.
Treats concealed and open speech as equal before the One who knows it, closely matching the hidden/disclosed boundary.
Affirms that Allah knows what people conceal and disclose.
States that Allah knows both what people hide and what they make public.
God knows best what is within persons, extending the focus from chests to inward moral state.
God knows the secret and what is still more hidden, sharpening the focus's unseen register.
His knowledge encompasses all things, a concise statement of the focus's comprehensive scope.
God knows declared speech and what people conceal.
God's knowledge of all that is in heaven and earth is established and recorded.
Explicitly names God knower of unseen and witnessed reality.
The Lord knows what chests conceal and what people disclose, directly paralleling the focus's final clause.
The Knower of the unseen misses nothing in heavens or earth, even the smallest particle.
God is named Originator and Knower of unseen and witnessed reality, broadening the focus's cosmic frame.
God knows the soul's inner whisper, a particularly close counterpart to knowledge of chest contents.
God knows people from their origin and while they are hidden in mothers' wombs.
God encompasses every secret consultation and all that is in heaven and earth.
Creation across the seven heavens and earth displays knowledge encompassing all things.
The Creator's intimate awareness grounds the claim that nothing within creation escapes Him.
God alone knows the unseen and controls its disclosure to messengers.
God recounts all matters with knowledge and was never absent from them.
The confession that the Lord encompasses everything in knowledge broadens the focus's scope.
God knows both their secret confiding and their private consultations.
God knows best what people allege or conceal, a narrower narrative instance of hidden knowledge.
God's sufficient witness is grounded in knowledge of everything in heavens and earth.
Whether speech is disclosed or concealed, God knows all things.
Knowledge of the Hour and of fruit emerging from its sheaths extends divine knowledge into hidden timing and formation.
God's deity in heaven and earth accompanies knowledge of the Hour, a broad cosmic parallel.
God knows what was in believers' hearts when He sent down tranquility.
God's knowledge of everything accompanies His sovereignty over the first, last, visible, and hidden.
